summary: Couch Investor compares two hated-but-undervalued names he owns, Netflix and Meta, arguing obvious buys only look obvious in hindsight. On Netflix (HOLD), he breaks down the report that it may open its app to Peacock and Fox One, debating whether Netflix becomes a distribution gatekeeper or is defensively bundling; the win would be more content and ad inventory without content spend, but it must not ruin Netflix's user-friendly experience. His DCF puts Netflix only ~10% undervalued on conservative 13%-to-10% revenue growth assumptions, so he is not adding until growth accelerates. Meta (BUY) is the 'obvious' one: down ~12% YTD despite faster growth and a cheaper multiple than Netflix, with a DCF implying ~50% upside to $861. He walks through Meta's $18B youth-safety settlement (10-year installments, 30% conditional on TikTok/YouTube matching teen protections like 1-hour daily limits and night mode) and argues it barely dents the business since teens are not the monetizable base. Upcoming Muse 'watermelon' model, new identity capabilities, subscriptions, and WhatsApp monetization are the catalysts. He also covers Rubrik (HOLD): a triple-beat quarter (38% revenue growth, 32.8% ARR growth) he owns but won't add to at these levels; and IREN, criticizing management's execution and undisclosed 'frontier AI lab' contract as failing the smell test.
title: The Most Obvious Buy In The Market Right Now
